title: gateway-bff composite route for the case screens is not specified
source: Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 14 and 45 (the gateway calls rwb-case and rwb-source-data in parallel and merges the answers); Template and Rules v1 §R5.5 DP-19
description: The architecture states that gateway-bff calls rwb-case and rwb-source-data in parallel, one hop each, and merges the two answers into the screen model, but no document gives the composite route path, the field merge order, the masking rules for customer fields or the timeout budget per screen. The app story can build the case side of the merge and the operations story can register the route target, but the composite contract itself is missing.
evidence: Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 14 notes (rwb-case IN and REST Access: authorise) and slide 45 (the case screen stays under 2 s because the gateway calls both services in parallel); no composite route document named in the sources read
proposed: Publish the gateway-bff composite route for SCR-02 and SCR-03 with its path, the parallel calls, the merge order, the masking rules and the 2 s budget, as part of RWB-PLT-N001-CON

title: Per-service login name for rwb-case is not specified
source: Template and Rules v1 §R4 (one login per service); Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 41 notes; legacy story RWB-E1-018 precondition on the service login
description: The target rule is one login per service and the legacy story names a single shared login. No source document gives the login name for rwb-case, its grant set or its secret reference. The stories therefore name it as a placeholder and the chart references it indirectly, so a build cannot create the login and its grants from the documents alone.
evidence: Template and Rules v1 §R4 and §R5.5 DP-02 name the rule but not the value; the legacy story precondition names the shared login only
proposed: Allocate the rwb-case login name and its grants (schema rwb_case only, no privilege on another schema) in the database story of RWB-SVC-P3 and record it in the service catalogue

title: Field-level OpenAPI schema of the case resource is not specified
source: Technical Specifications by Module v5 P3 T3.1 (field types and lengths) and T-A.2 (operation inventory); API Specification v4
description: The TSD gives the field names, types and lengths of the case, account and party tables, and the legacy story gives the response field lists, but no document gives the field-level OpenAPI schema: the required flags per operation, the page and sort parameter set of GET /cases, the pattern of caseNo and the exact error codes per operation. The contract baseline can fix the names and the envelope, not the field-level detail.
evidence: TSD P3 v3 T3.1 field tables; legacy story section 12 endpoint table; no OpenAPI 3.1 fragment in the sources read
proposed: Agree the field-level schema in the baseline review of RWB-P3-E1018-CON with the consuming teams, and record it in the rwb-case API file

title: Deployment topology detail for rwb-case is not specified
source: Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 41 and 44 (one service, one chart, one pipeline; Schedules per service); Template and Rules v1 §R5.5 DP-10 and DP-15
description: The architecture fixes one chart, one pipeline and Schedules in the owning service, but no document gives the cluster names, node pools, replica counts, resource requests and limits, zone spread, ingress class or the probe paths and timings of rwb-case. The chart can expose them as values, but the environment values themselves are missing.
evidence: Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 41 notes (one Helm chart, one pipeline) and slide 44 notes (Schedules per service); no deployment topology document in the sources read
proposed: Publish the rwb-case deployment topology and the environment values with the platform template, and keep them as values files rather than chart defaults

title: The per-service database login name of rwb-case is not specified
source: Recovery Workbench Microservice Story Template and Rules v1 §R4 (one login per service, DP-02); TSD P3 Case and workflow v3 T6.2; legacy RWB-E1-019 used the shared recovery_svc login
section: R4 service naming; T6.2 authentication and authorization; section 13 Solution plan
description: The target model gives every service its own database login, but no source document names the rwb-case login. The legacy story grants to the shared recovery_svc login only. Every grant, migration owner and runbook step in this legacy key therefore needs a name that does not yet exist.
evidence: Template and Rules §R4 lists 'login per service' without a value; legacy RWB-E1-019 §3 and §13 name recovery_svc; TSD P3 v3 T6.2 names no login.
proposed: ACE DB allocates one login per service before the wave 1 DB builds; until then every document writes 'the rwb-case login (DP-02)' and the grant scripts take the name from a parameter.

title: The column-level split of the legacy role and permission tables between rwb-case and rwb-access is not defined
source: Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 14 and 41 (P4 owns Recovery roles as data, scope, masking policy, DoA table); ownership map entries role, permission, masking_rule, delegation_limit; legacy RWB-E1-019 §11 reads role.role_code
section: 2 Business rationale; 10 Authority; 11 Data; 12.7 Tables owned
description: The ownership map puts role, permission, masking_rule and delegation_limit in rwb-access (P4), and the legacy story reads and writes ROLE and TEAM rows inside one schema. No source states which columns of the legacy role and TEAM tables move to rwb-access, which stay in rwb-case reference data, or how a queue row's role code is validated after the move.
evidence: Ownership map: role and permission owner P4 with basis Arch v5 slides 14 and 41; TSD P3 v3 T3.2 keeps TEAM and ROLE as LOV-REF-TABLE codes while TSD P4 v3 declares the role table; legacy RWB-E1-019 BR1, BR9 and §11.
proposed: Roles, permissions, scope, masking and delegation stay with rwb-access; rwb-case keeps TEAM as reference data and keeps only role_code as a code, validated at load time over the rwb-access authorise contract (DP-08). Confirm the column list with P4 in the RWB-P4-E1037-CON contract.

title: The column-level definition of queue measures and of the remaining list-of-values columns is not specified
source: Legacy RWB-E1-019 §11 (only lov_value.lov_code DF-REF-028 and lov_value.value_code DF-REF-029 are given); FSD P3 v4 FEAT-CWC-18 names the measures without columns; TSD P3 v3 T3.1 defines queue_measure DF-RPT-020 to DF-RPT-030 and no lov_value field list
description: The split gives rwb-case a queue measure table and the lists of values, but the legacy story carries no measure column and only two list columns. The technical specification gives a measure snapshot, so the measure columns can be taken from it, yet the rest of the list-of-values column set and the intended measure grain (per queue, per day, per team) are not stated anywhere.
evidence: Legacy RWB-E1-019 §11 reads DF-REF-028 and DF-REF-029 only; TSD P3 v3 T3.1 queue_measure has DF-RPT-020 to DF-RPT-030 and LOV-SNAPSHOT-STATUS; no source defines the remaining lov_value columns.
proposed: Take the queue_measure columns from TSD P3 v3 T3.1 and the lov_value columns from the reference-data story (DF-REF-028 and DF-REF-029 at minimum); any further column is added by a later migration, not by a guess.

title: The queues reference-load template format is not specified
source: Legacy RWB-E1-019 §4 step 1 and §12 (multipart file, table QUEUE or QUEUE_MEMBER, validFrom); TSD P3 v3 gives no workbook layout
section: 4 Flow; 11 Data; 12.1 REST operations provided; 14 Validation and messages
description: The legacy story names two sheets and the row-level checks, but not the column order, the required columns per sheet, the header names or the cell formats of the Queues template. The load operation and the database columns are therefore defined while the file that feeds them is not.
evidence: Legacy RWB-E1-019 §4 step 1 ('fills the Queues template (sheets QUEUE and QUEUE_MEMBER)') and §12 request row; no template attachment or column list in the FSD or TSD P3.
proposed: Publish the template as an xlsx workbook with one header row per sheet, a column per queue and queue_member field, and one check per required column; the contract in RWB-P3-E1019-CON accepts it as multipart and does not fix the column order in v1.

title: The rollback and verify operations of reference loads sit outside the rwb-case operation set given for this legacy key
source: Ownership map (POST /admin/reference-loads/{loadId}/rollback and .../verify, owner P3); legacy RWB-E1-019 §12 and AC2, AC7 use rollback
section: 4 Flow step 8; 12.1 REST operations provided; 19 Out of scope
description: Two legacy criteria and one flow step depend on a rollback call, and the ownership map lists the rollback and verify paths as P3, but the rwb-case operation set stated for this service excludes them. The app story therefore keeps the behaviour and tests it against a fake, while no published operation of this legacy key covers it. A reader cannot tell whether the rollback is rwb-case work in a later story or belongs to rwb-access.
evidence: Ownership map: POST /admin/reference-loads/{loadId}/rollback and .../verify owner P3 with the reference-data ruling; legacy RWB-E1-019 §12 'new endpoint, see additions' and §5 X4, X6; the rwb-case provided-operation list for this service does not include them.
proposed: Keep rollback and verify with rwb-case as the ownership map says and publish them in a later rwb-case contract story; until then RWB-P3-E1019-APP tests AC2 and AC7 against the contract fake and does not claim the operation in its section 12.

title: The approver authority for a queues load is assumed, not confirmed
source: Legacy RWB-E1-019 §3 ('assumed grant; DL01') and §10; FSD P3 v4 A2.6.3.3 names the roles without the grant
description: The legacy story assumes that RW-TEAMMGR, acting for the Shared operations table owner, holds Reference data A and may approve a queues version. The role exists as data; the grant is an assumption carried from DL01 and is not confirmed by any BRD, FSD or ownership row, so the approval step of the load cannot be authorised with certainty in the target.
evidence: Legacy RWB-E1-019 §3 bullet 3 and §10 row for RW-TEAMMGR, both marked assumed; FSD P3 v4 A2.6.3.3 lists Reference data administrator, center of excellence analyst and team manager without grants.
proposed: Confirm with the access owner that RW-TEAMMGR holds Reference data A for the TEAM, QUEUE and QUEUE_MEMBER tables and record the grant as rwb-access data; the contract keeps 403 MSG-P4-002 as the refusal.

title: The rwb-case service login name is not given in any source
source: Arch v5 Text Extract v1 slide 41 (one schema and one login per service); TSD P3 v3 T2.5 (worker identity SY-CASEWF only)
description: The template fixes one login per service in the ACE database, but no source document names the rwb-case login. The stories cannot deploy the worker, connect the chart to the database or hand credentials to the contract fakes without the name, so the placeholder is used in all three slices of RWB-P3-E1020.
evidence: Arch v5 slide 41 gives schema rwb_case and 'a login per service' with no name; TSD P3 v3 T2.5 names only the worker identity SY-CASEWF and the evaluator identity SY-RULES; no naming convention for service logins is written down in the Architecture or TSD extracts.
proposed: Allocate the login together with the schema in the 19-schema list, derive it from the schema name, store it in Key Vault, and record the name in the Service Catalog and the RWB-PLT-DB stories before the first deployment.

title: The source of the caseload cap is not fixed: parameter row or reference data
source: Legacy RWB-E1-020 section 8 BR3 and section 11; TSD P3 v3 T3.1 (queue.capacity_cap, queue_member.capacity); FSD P3 v4 A2.6 AC-ALT-P3-006-02 (queue_member.capacity 40)
description: The legacy story reads the cap from queue.capacity_cap and queue_member.capacity and cites DL23 for the values, while the same story treats every value a business person may change as a versioned data row and the parameter catalog is the standard place for limits. No source says whether the cap of 150 is a parameter_value row, a reference_row of the QUEUE and QUEUE_MEMBER tables, or both, and the contract cannot fix the field source until it is decided.
evidence: Legacy RWB-E1-020 section 13 'Configuration and reference data' lists the caps as DL23 reference values and the parameters as allocation.exception.queue.code and allocation.deviation.queue.code only; TSD P3 v3 T3.1 declares capacity_cap on queue and capacity on queue_member; TSD P3 v3 T3.1 also declares parameter_catalog and parameter_value for limits and thresholds.
proposed: Keep the cap as versioned reference data on queue.capacity_cap and queue_member.capacity, as the legacy data model does, and add a parameter key only if a product-level override is wanted; state the ruling in the Reference Data and Parameters design.

title: The exact cadence of the rebalancing trigger is not defined for rwb-case
source: Arch v5 Text Extract v1 slide 44 (JOB-06 rebalancing 06:30, mechanism Schedule); FSD P3 v4 A2.17 (JOB-06 runs)
description: The job map gives 06:30 for JOB-06 and names a Temporal Schedule, but it does not say whether rebalancing runs before or after DailyCaseRun, whether it is a separate Schedule or a step inside the morning run, or what happens when the run for the business date has not finished. The stories register the activity and the Schedule and must leave the expression as a value, so the operations team needs a ruling before the first live run.
evidence: Arch v5 slide 44: 'JOB-06 Rebalancing, 06:30, rwb-case, Schedule'. Arch v5 slide 29 lists the overnight chain with case creation and allocation but not JOB-06. FSD P3 v4 A2.17 says only 'JOB-06 runs' and gives no relation to JOB-02 or JOB-03.
owner_role: Business owner, Shared operations; platform team, Temporal
proposed: Run JOB-06 as its own Temporal Schedule at 06:30 Asia/Bangkok, after DailyCaseRun has finished, with overlap policy SKIP and a catch-up window; confirm the order with the operations owner and record it in the Temporal Workflow and Activity Catalog.

title: The deployment topology of the rwb-case allocation worker is not specified
source: Arch v5 Text Extract v1 slides 2, 8 and 11 (api and worker deployment per service, KEDA on backlog); no sizing or archive detail
description: The architecture states that every service has an api and a worker deployment, scales workers on task-queue backlog and keeps Temporal history in its own database, but no source gives replica bounds, node pool placement, connection budget per service or where closed run history is archived. The deployment story must expose them as chart values without a fixed answer, and SIT has to produce the numbers.
evidence: Arch v5 slide 2 'Each has an api and a worker deployment'; slide 8 'each an api and a worker deployment'; slide 11 'KEDA scales workers on backlog'; slide 9 'Temporal keeps its own persistence database; retention 30 days for closed workflows' with no sizing. The TSD P3 v3 T2.5 table gives connection and configuration values but no replicas or node pool.
proposed: Expose replicas, autoscaling bounds, node pool, connection pool size and the history archive as chart values with documented defaults, record the SIT findings in the Service Template Specification, and let the platform observability story own the capacity review.

title: Per-service database login name for rwb-case is not specified
source: Template and Rules v1 section R4 (login per service) and section R5.5 DP-02
description: No source names the database login of rwb-case. Template and Rules R4 requires one login per service and DP-02 replaces the shared monolith login, but neither the Architecture v5 extract nor the TSD P3 names the login, its owner or its grant set. The stories and the chart use the placeholder phrase "the rwb-case login (DP-02)".
evidence: Architecture v5 slide 41 gives the schema rwb_case and says each service has its own login without naming it; TSD P3 v3 T1 and T6.2 name roles and schemas but no database login; Template and Rules R4 lists "login per service" only.
proposed: The ACE DB team names the login and its grant set in the P3 DB story and in RWB-PLT-NF06-DB, and the chart takes it by vault secret reference. This run keeps the placeholder until then.

title: No source names who may override a transfer refused by a rule, the cap check or the status check
source: RWB E1 021 Transfer rules and engine v1 v2 (sections 5, 7, 10)
description: The legacy story refuses a transfer in five ways (no reason, owner at the cap, closed case, hold on a hold, no matching rule) and names no role, endpoint or procedure that may override a refusal. The Epic 2 transfer screen and the Business Rules and Routing Logic extract add no override rule either.
evidence: RWB-E1-021 exception paths X2, X3, X4, X9, X10 state "nothing changes" and name no override; section 10 Authority lists only who may transfer; the FSD P3 v4 A2.10 validation rules VR-P3-010-1 and VR-P3-010-2 stop at the refusal.
proposed: Confirm with the business owner in the Epic 2 transfer screen story (RWB-E2-012). This run assumes no override path in Epic 1: a refused transfer changes nothing and the caller retries with another target.

title: Ownership and change control of the transfer reason list are not specified
source: TSD P3 v3 T3.2 (LOV-TRANSFER-REASON) and the Business Requirements (DL23)
description: LOV-TRANSFER-REASON is defined as the six codes R01 to R06 with their meanings, and RWB-E1-021 says RW-REFADM loads the list through RWB-E1-043. No source says who owns the list, who approves adding or retiring a code, or whether the list is reference data of rwb-case or of the business. The contract therefore references the list and does not enumerate it.
evidence: TSD P3 v3 T3.2 lists LOV-TRANSFER-REASON R01 to R06; TSD P3 v3 T3.2 LOV-REF-TABLE includes TRANSFER; Template and Rules R3 default ruling gives reference data to P3; RWB-E1-021 section 13 says RW-REFADM loads the list and section 3 cites DL23, without naming an owner.
proposed: P3 owns the list as reference data under the R-PREC default ruling and DP-07, and the business owner of DL23 approves every addition or retirement through the reference-load approve operation of rwb-case.

title: Deployment topology of the transfer capability is not specified
source: Template and Rules v1 section R4 and Architecture v5 slides 4 and 20
description: The sources fix the service facts (schema, base path, topic, task queue, package) and say each service has an api and a worker deployment, but no source gives the cluster, node pool, replica counts per environment, ingress host, resource limits or the pod disruption budget of rwb-case.
evidence: Architecture v5 slide 4 says every service has an api and a worker deployment and slide 20 repeats it; Template and Rules R4 lists the service facts only; the TSD P3 v3 non-functional section gives no topology.
proposed: The platform team publishes cluster, node pool, replica counts, ingress host, resource limits and the disruption budget as chart values; the chart ships no environment default and the two-replica starting values are proposals.

title: The per-service database login name for rwb-case is not given
source: Template and Rules v1 R4 (login per service); Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 41; TSD P3 v3 T3.0 and T6.2
section: RWB-P3-E1023-APP section 3 Preconditions, section 10 Authority, section 13 Solution plan; RWB-P3-E1023-CON section 3 Preconditions
description: Every service has its own database login with grants on its own schema only, but no source names the login of rwb-case. The legacy identity name recovery_svc is retired by DP-02, so the read contract, the Flyway grant and the deployment cannot name the login.
evidence: Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 41 and slide 9 note each service has its own database login with grants on its own schema only; Template and Rules v1 R4 lists a login per service without a value; DP-02 replaces recovery_svc with one login per service; TSD P3 v3 T6.2 names the service identities SY-CASEWF and SY-RULES but no database login.
proposed: Write the login as the rwb-case login (DP-02) and take the name from RWB-PLT-DB when it is issued; grant SELECT, INSERT and UPDATE on schema rwb_case only.

title: The gateway-bff composite route specification for SCR-03 is not given
source: Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 10 walkthrough note; Template and Rules v1 R5.5 DP-19; RWB-PLT-N001-CON
section: RWB-P3-E1023-APP section 3 Preconditions, section 5 Exception paths X11, section 13 Solution plan, section 15 Screens and states; RWB-P3-E1023-CON section 3 Preconditions, section 12.8 Contract fakes
description: The case record screen is served as a gateway-bff composite route that calls rwb-case and rwb-source-data in parallel and merges the answers. No source fixes the route path, the merge rules, the per-call timeout ownership or the partial-failure behaviour of the merge, so the case block shape and the screen model cannot be closed.
evidence: Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 10 note: the browser calls /api/recovery/cases/{id}, gateway-bff calls rwb-case GET /v1/cases/{id} and rwb-source-data GET /v1/customers/{id} and /v1/accounts/{id} in parallel and merges the two answers; Template and Rules v1 R5.5 DP-19 gives only 'gateway-bff composite route' and H RWB-PLT-N001-CON.
proposed: Publish the route with its path, the parallel call set, the merge field map, the 2 s budget split and the partial-failure rule in RWB-PLT-N001-CON; keep the five rwb-case read operations unchanged.

title: The exact field masking contract shape is not given
source: RWB-P4-E1039-CON contract line; Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 14 rwb-access contract; DP-08; DL26
section: RWB-P3-E1023-APP section 3 Preconditions, section 13 Solution plan; RWB-P3-E1023-CON section 7 AC4, section 12.8 Contract fakes
description: Personal fields are filled from the masked or the clear view column according to the masking rule in force, but no source gives the request and response shape of the masking contract: whether the policy is keyed by view field ID, by DTO field, or by both, and how the masked and clear columns are named in the answer. The document therefore marks the hook without fixing its payload.
evidence: Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 14 lists GET /masking-policies on rwb-access with no payload; DP-08 names the authorise contract and the guard library only; the legacy story RWB-E1-023 section 12 names FieldMasker and the field IDs DF-ACE-073, DF-ACE-074, DF-ACE-078 and DF-ACE-079 without a payload shape.
proposed: Publish the masking policy request and response in RWB-P4-E1039-CON keyed by view field ID with a masked flag and the source column per field, and let rwb-case send the field list it read.

title: The timeline paging and the interaction ledger read operation are not given
source: Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 15 rwb-source-data contract; DP-18; TSD P3 v3 API-P3-003
section: RWB-P3-E1023-APP section 8 BR13, section 12.2 REST operations consumed; RWB-P3-E1023-CON section 11 Data, section 12.1 REST operations provided, section 12.2 REST operations consumed
description: The case timeline merges rwb-case state changes with the interaction ledger now owned by rwb-source-data. The P1 contract line lists customers, accounts, collateral, payments, freshness and the business-day call but no interaction read, and no source gives the timeline page size or its default order beyond ordered by time. The page and size parameters exist on the legacy contract only.
evidence: Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 15 lists the rwb-source-data IN operations with no interaction read; Template and Rules v1 R3 default ruling and DP-18 move the ledger to rwb-source-data; TSD P3 v3 API-P3-003 gives query type, from and to with a TimelinePage and no paging values; the legacy story RWB-E1-023 section 12 gives page and size on the interactions endpoint.
proposed: Add the interaction read operation to the rwb-source-data contract with its path and its page and size parameters, and fix the timeline default order as occurred_at descending with the page size taken from a parameter.
